name: AMFI - Amsterdam Fashion Institute (English programme)
about: Fashion from designing and making garments to branding and selling them, with a specialisation in Fashion & Design, Fashion & Branding or Fashion & Management and hands-on industry projects.

name: AMSIB - International Business
about: A broad international business degree with five majors, such as International Marketing and Sales or Global Business Communication, plus a compulsory exchange, internship and thesis.

name: European School of Physiotherapy
about: An intensive three-year physiotherapy degree in English that mixes science, practical skills and clinical internships in varied healthcare settings, taught in small international groups.

name: Sport Studies (track ISMB)
about: Management and business applied to sport, with entrepreneurial projects and three internships at international sport organisations over the four years.

name: Liberal Arts and Sciences
about: Broad interdisciplinary study across the sciences, social sciences and humanities with a major in one of the three, in classes of at most 25, on a residential campus at Amsterdam Science Park.

name: Applied Mathematics
about: Mathematical modelling, programming and data science applied to real problems from companies, with AI used as a tool; two internships, and a data science specialisation from year 3.

name: Applied Physics
about: Physics theory, lab experiments and projects on problems such as energy, hospital equipment and sound, in a small programme on the TU/e campus in Eindhoven.

name: Applied Science - Chemistry and Chemical Engineering
about: Chemistry, chemical engineering and biology taught together as one toolkit for work on medicines, sustainable materials, clean water or diagnostics, in a small programme on the TU/e campus.

name: Automotive Engineering
about: Mechanics, electronics and software applied to vehicles: you design, build and test them, with half a day a week in the workshop in year 1 before you choose a direction.

name: Circus and Performance Art
about: Professional circus training with a flexible curriculum built around your own artistic goals, in a dedicated training hall in Tilburg with internationally qualified teachers.

name: Communication - International Communication Management
about: How organisations plan and manage communication across cultures and borders: communication strategy, intercultural understanding and working with people in diverse contexts.

name: Dance - Dance Arts in Context
about: Contemporary, contemporary urban or choreography: you develop your own dance style and choreographic skills and explore current trends, in an international setting in Tilburg.

name: Electrical and Electronic Engineering
about: Designing the electronics inside devices, from patient monitors to electric cars and energy systems, with a focus on sustainable solutions.

name: Finance & Control
about: Finance, accounting, risk management and strategic decision-making for businesses, with company projects and classes of at most 30 in Venlo. Formerly International Finance & Control.

name: ICT: Information & Communication Technology
about: A broad ICT bachelor's: a common start, then one of 13 specialisations such as AI, cyber security or software development, built on real-life projects.

name: Industrial Design Engineering
about: Product design covering form, use, function, production and market value, with sustainability and social impact built in, through design assignments with companies in Venlo.

name: Industrial Engineering and Management
about: Improving and managing the processes of technical organisations, with projects for Brainport companies such as ASML and Philips and a personal coach throughout.

name: Information Technology
about: Software and AI development in teams for real clients: you analyse complex problems and build digital solutions, with attention to people and society, in Venlo.

name: International Business
about: A BBA covering international business, culture, marketing, finance, supply chain and HR, with classmates from across the world, in Eindhoven or Venlo.

name: Logistics Engineering
about: Logistics processes, data analysis and teamwork, with internships and company projects from the start in Venlo; prepares you for engineer or analyst roles.

name: Logistics Management
about: Preparation for management roles in logistics, with a focus on sustainability and data, internships and projects, and a personal mentor, in Venlo.

name: Marketing Management
about: Market analysis, consumer behaviour, online channels, sales and product development, with two six-month internships worldwide and classes of at most 30 in Venlo.

name: Marketing Management - Digital Business Concepts
about: A mix of digital, marketing and business: you learn to design, develop and market digital products and business models with data, on assignments from companies, in Tilburg.

name: Mechanical Engineering
about: Applying physics to design and build mechanical systems, structures and machines, with in-depth study of materials, lab work and industry projects.

name: Mechatronics
about: Designing control systems for robot-controlled products and machines, mixing mechanical, electrical and software engineering in projects, in Eindhoven or Venlo.

name: Medical Imaging and Radiation Therapy
about: Training to work with medical imaging and radiation therapy equipment: anatomy, imaging studies, radiation safety and patient care, in small classes in Eindhoven.

name: Music - Conservatory of Music Tilburg
about: Classical or jazz music in a broad musical context, with teachers active on the music scene and ensemble projects that connect you with professionals, in Tilburg.

name: Physiotherapy
about: All aspects of physiotherapy, from treating injuries to preventing them, with anatomy, neurology and physiology, hands-on practice and real patients, in small classes.

name: Applied Computer Science
about: Software that runs on devices, machines and systems rather than only on screens: the programme combines software and hardware over four years, moving from foundations to a specialisation and professional practice.

name: Classical Music
about: Train as a versatile classical performer and teacher on one of some two dozen instruments or voice, with orchestra and chamber-music stage experience, pedagogy, entrepreneurship and work placements.

name: Creative Media & Game Technologies
about: Design and build games and interactive experiences with Unity, Unreal Engine, AR/VR and virtual production, learning through projects for real clients rather than exams.

name: Design
about: A broad design degree: in the first year you try all six majors (graphic & interaction, illustration & animation, spatial, time-based, product, OffRoad) before choosing one, working through studio, lab and theory classes.

name: Electrical and Electronic Engineering
about: Design, build and programme electronic solutions in hands-on projects for real clients, specialising from year 3 in Mechatronics, Sensors & Smart Systems or Energy & Power Electronics.

name: Fine Art
about: A studio-based route to becoming an independent visual artist, where making and thinking go together across media, with tutors who are practising artists and options for exchange, minors and research projects.

name: International Business
about: Business fundamentals (marketing, finance, supply chain, HR) with a compulsory year abroad: a semester at one of 120+ partner universities plus an international placement, and a foreign language from five.

name: International Business (3-year)
about: The same International Business degree compressed into three years for pre-university diplomas, with a compulsory year abroad (partner-university semester and international internship) and a heavier self-study load.

name: International Communication
about: How stories, news and campaigns shape opinion: PR and marketing, crisis communication and public affairs, consultancy and media writing, with a second year spent as a consultant on real client briefs.

name: International Facility Management
about: How organisations run their services and spaces: semesters alternate between services and (work)space management, with hospitality, health and sustainability in view. One of two English-taught FM degrees in the Netherlands.

name: International Finance & Control
about: Business finance for international organisations: a first year of financial and economic basics, then business economics and information provision, practised in projects for real clients.

name: Jazz
about: Become a professional jazz musician through weekly lessons with Dutch and international jazz players, with performance on stage from the first year alongside theory.

name: Marketing Management
about: Find out what customers need and want and how to win them for a brand, through theory and project work for real companies in an international classroom.

name: Mechanical Engineering
about: A three-year engineering bachelor built on real projects from day one, which gives direct entry to Hanze's European Master in Renewable Energy or Smart Systems Engineering: an MSc in four and a half years.

name: Physiotherapy
about: Help people with movement problems move well again, combining medical-biological knowledge, treatment methods, behavioural psychology, communication and entrepreneurship, with much practice on peers and in clinics.

name: Popular Culture
about: Make interdisciplinary performance work for audiences as a performer, writer/composer or visualiser/designer, learning in a production-house model with cultural institutions in Leeuwarden.

name: Sport Studies
about: A three-year degree on the role of sport in health, the economy and society, working on real challenges with professional sports organisations throughout.

name: African Studies
about: Africa's history, languages, literature and societies studied across the humanities; you learn Swahili and spend a semester of year two studying in an African country.

name: Archaeology
about: How past societies lived, reconstructed from material remains, with theory in class and hands-on fieldwork; Leiden's large archaeology faculty lets you specialise by region and period.

name: Arts, Media and Society
about: Contemporary visual art, from painting and photography to installation, performance and digital media, and how art connects with society, media and issues such as climate and conflict.

name: Cultural Anthropology and Development Sociology
about: Why people live and think differently across the world, studied through theory plus your own fieldwork, internships and ethnographic film-making, with themes like inequality and climate justice.

name: Data Science and Artificial Intelligence
about: Computer science, maths, statistics and machine learning combined, building strong programming foundations and AI skills, taught at Leiden's computer science institute (LIACS).

name: Dutch Studies
about: Dutch language, literature, history and society for international students, starting from any level of Dutch; classes are taught partly in Dutch from the first semester.

name: English Language and Culture
about: English in all its forms, from medieval texts to contemporary literature, film and linguistics, alongside advanced training in your own written and spoken English.

name: International Studies
about: One of eight world regions studied through its history, politics, economics and culture, while you learn a major language of that region; taught in The Hague.

name: Liberal Arts and Sciences: Global Challenges (Leiden University College)
about: Global challenges such as peace, justice, sustainability and development, studied in small interdisciplinary classes on a residential campus in The Hague before you pick a major.

name: Linguistics
about: How languages are built, compared and change, including endangered languages, with specialisations such as descriptive and comparative Indo-European linguistics. No other languages needed.

name: Philosophy: Global and Comparative Perspectives
about: Philosophy's big questions studied by comparing Western thought with Indian, East Asian, African and Arabic traditions side by side, rather than as separate options.

name: Political Science: International Relations and Organisations
about: Diplomacy, conflict, international institutions and transnational problems studied as political science, in The Hague among UN bodies, embassies and NGOs.

name: Psychology (International Bachelor in Psychology)
about: Psychology as a science, from brain and cognition to social, clinical and developmental psychology, with research methods and statistics throughout; the English track of Leiden's psychology bachelor.

name: Science for Sustainable Societies
about: Sustainability problems tackled across natural science, social science and governance, with practical skills such as coding, GIS and working with stakeholders.

name: Security Studies
about: Terrorism, cybercrime, crises and conflict studied in their political, historical and social context, with a practical focus on how governments and organisations respond; taught in The Hague.

name: South and Southeast Asian Studies
about: The history, cultures and politics of South and Southeast Asia, studied alongside a language of the region: Hindi, Sanskrit, Tibetan or Indonesian.

name: Urban Studies
about: Cities and their problems, such as sustainability, diversity, safety and health, studied across the humanities, social sciences, science and law, using The Hague as the case.

name: American Studies
about: The United States studied through its politics, society, history, literature, media and language, in full English immersion, with the option of a semester in the US or an internship. A specialisation of English Language and Culture.

name: Artificial Intelligence
about: AI with a special focus on understanding and simulating the brain, taught alongside the Donders Institute and the Max Planck Institute for Psycholinguistics on campus; programming is taught from scratch.

name: Arts and Culture Studies
about: Visual arts, literature, (pop) music, film, television and theatre studied side by side in small international classes, learning to write sharp reviews and to curate art with its audience in mind.

name: Biology
about: A broad biology degree across seven domains, from molecules to ecosystems, with heavy lab and field time (30+ contact hours in year 1) and internships at Radboud's research institutes.

name: Chemistry
about: Chemistry with a solid theoretical base and extensive lab training, working on new medicines and sustainable materials with high-tech research facilities such as the high-field magnet lab.

name: Computing Science
about: Programming built on its mathematical foundations, with strong cyber security and AI groups; you build software for real clients in the student company GiPHouse and try new devices in the lab.

name: Economics and Business Economics
about: Economics seen through accounting, finance and international economics and policy; after the first year you choose one of these as your specialisation. Same content as the Dutch-taught version.

name: English Language and Culture
about: A research-based degree joining English linguistics, literature, culture, society and history, with language-acquisition courses from day one and the option to study abroad or intern.

name: International Business Administration
about: Marketing, HRM, strategy and other business processes studied as one system in an international context, with a focus on responsible and sustainable organisations and a flexible third-year semester.

name: International Business Communication
about: How organisations communicate across languages and cultures: intercultural and professional communication, scenario-based projects, and academic English or Spanish. The English-taught track of Communication and Information Studies.

name: Molecular Life Sciences
about: Chemistry, biology and medical science combined to work on molecular solutions to medical problems, with lectures, computer practicals and hands-on lab experiments from the start.

name: Natural Sciences
about: Physics, chemistry and biology integrated into one programme with mathematics, with access to facilities such as the FELIX laser lab and the High Field Magnet Laboratory.

name: Philosophy, Politics and Society
about: An issue-led philosophy degree: the curriculum is built around themes such as ecological crisis, the future of technology, identity politics and the global political order, and the ideas behind them.

name: Psychology
about: A broad psychology degree tied to research in brain and cognition, development and mental health, and behaviour and environment, with electives from year 2 and an optional semester abroad in year 3.

name: International Business
about: Business, languages and professional skills in three learning lines, a specialisation in Marketing, Commerce, Supply Chain or Organisation & Change, and exchange and internships in years 3-4.

name: Fine Art
about: Your own art practice developed through artistic research and concept work across autonomous, social and commercial settings, with a focus on digital technology and public space.

name: Graphic Design
about: Shaping information into visual communication with traditional and cross-media techniques, building your own design approach through creative research and critical thinking.

name: American Studies
about: The United States from many angles at once: its politics, history, literature, popular culture, race relations and religions, and its ties with the rest of the Americas. Taught in small seminars.

name: Applied Mathematics
about: Using mathematics to model and simulate real systems, from vehicle dynamics to energy networks, combining proofs with programming and simulation. The first year is shared with Mathematics, so you can still switch after it.

name: Applied Physics
about: Physics aimed at technology: the fundamentals plus design, nanotechnology, new materials and control engineering, for work in energy, medical technology and materials. Taught next to Physics, so you need not choose between them straight away.

name: Art History
about: Visual art, architecture, cities and landscapes studied together and in their environmental context, mixing historical, theoretical and practice-based courses, with an excursion abroad to a city such as Berlin, London or Florence.

name: Artificial Intelligence
about: How intelligence works in people and machines, combining machine learning, programming, cognitive psychology, neuroscience, linguistics and philosophy. Specialise in computational neuroscience, hybrid intelligence, language and AI, machine learning or robotics.

name: Arts, Culture and Media
about: Film, music or theatre (with literature or visual arts as a possible second art form) studied in depth, with how art is made, funded and received; choose a framework in arts policy and cultural entrepreneurship or in analysis and criticism.

name: Astronomy
about: Stars, galaxies, planetary systems and cosmology on a solid base of physics and mathematics, with the university's own observatory and links to the SRON and ASTRON space and radio astronomy institutes. You can switch to Physics or Mathematics in year one.

name: Biology
about: Living systems from molecules to ecosystems, combined with maths, physics and chemistry. A broad first semester, then a major in ecology and evolution, molecular life sciences, behaviour and neurosciences, or biomedical sciences (partly at the UMCG hospital).

name: Biomedical Engineering
about: Engineering for healthcare: medical imaging, robotics, biomaterials and tissue engineering, on problems such as longer-lasting heart valves or automated MRI analysis. Run with the University Medical Center Groningen, where some courses are taught.

name: Chemical Engineering
about: Designing and optimising large-scale processes for fuels, food, medicines and materials, through thermodynamics, transport phenomena and reactor engineering. Most of year one is shared with Chemistry, and you can switch between the two during that year.

name: Chemistry
about: Organic, inorganic and physical chemistry with a lot of lab research, then a specialisation in smart materials, chemistry of life, or sustainable chemistry and energy. You can switch to Chemical Engineering during the first year.

name: Communication and Information Studies
about: Why communication succeeds or fails, across text, talk, images, digital media and generative AI, drawing on linguistics, psychology, media studies and marketing. You design and test improvements for real cases in corporate, health and intercultural communication.

name: Computing Science
about: The theory and practice of computing: programming in several languages, algorithms, mathematical foundations, software and systems design and data analysis, with room for creative projects and research in fields such as bioinformatics and astronomy.

name: Data Science and Society
about: Programming, data analysis and machine learning taught together with the law, ethics and politics of data, with projects for real organisations on the small Leeuwarden campus. In year two you specialise in AI and Society or in Cognitive Technology.

name: Econometrics and Operations Research
about: Mathematical modelling of economic and business problems, combining econometrics, operations research, actuarial science and mathematical economics, with a simulation game in which you run a company in all three years.

name: Economics and Business Economics
about: Economic tools for questions such as inequality, growth and climate impact, with strong data skills. Specialise in Economics, Business Economics, or International Economics and Sustainable Development; year three leaves room for a minor, internship or exchange.

name: English Language and Culture
about: English literature, culture and linguistics from medieval origins to today, across Britain, North America and the wider English-speaking world, taught in small classes; the oldest English programme in the Netherlands.

name: European Languages, Cultures and Politics
about: Europe's politics, cultures and languages, with intensive study of one major language (German, English, French, Italian, Dutch, Russian, Spanish or Swedish) towards near-native level, and a profile in language, culture or politics from year two.

name: Global Politics and Sustainability
about: Climate, biodiversity and energy transitions seen through politics, economics and society, with a specialisation in Planet or Politics and a Living Lab project for outside partners, in a small programme in Leeuwarden. Formerly Global Responsibility & Leadership.

name: History
about: The international track of History: a survey from Antiquity to the present, then political, cultural, economic and social history centred on a world region you choose, ending in your own research and thesis. All classes are in English.

name: Human Geography and Planning
about: Why cities and regions develop differently and how to plan better places, combining economic, cultural and population geography, real estate studies and planning, with statistics taking a large share of the programme.

name: Industrial Engineering and Management
about: An engineering degree with management: about two-thirds technical courses (maths, physics, chemistry, programming) and one-third business, applied to production, supply chains, logistics and energy systems.

name: Information Science
about: Applied AI, data science and language technology: building and evaluating software that processes large amounts of text and data, with attention to human and societal needs. Taught in English at the Faculty of Arts.

name: International and European Law
about: International, European and comparative law rather than one national legal system, with an optional Technology Law track from year two and a semester abroad for every student. It does not qualify you to practise law in the Netherlands.

name: International Business
about: International business seen through management, finance, marketing, ethics, sociology, psychology and economics, with real company cases and a third year for exchange, an internship or a minor. About 40% of students come from abroad.

name: International Relations and International Organization
about: International politics studied through history, economics, law and international organisations, plus training in a modern foreign language and a minor of your choice, in a programme running for three decades.

name: Liberal Arts and Sciences
about: University College Groningen's small liberal arts programme: explore several disciplines, then major in Humanities, Sciences or Social Sciences, with team projects for outside partners and much class discussion. Starts in September or February.

name: Life Science and Technology
about: Life at the molecular scale, combining biology, chemistry, physics and pharmacology: drug design, cellular imaging and bioinformatics, with lab work from year one. Two broad years come before you specialise.

name: Mathematics
about: Pure mathematics in depth: algebra, topology, analysis, probability, number theory and dynamical systems, with a focus on rigorous proof. The first year is shared with Applied Mathematics, so you can switch without delay.

name: Media Studies
about: The social and informative role of media, from print and television to platforms and search engines, studied comparatively in their political, economic and cultural contexts with social-science methods, plus professional skills for media work.

name: Physics
about: Mechanics, electromagnetism and quantum physics with plenty of lab work, then a specialisation in biophysics and medical physics, energy and environmental physics, nanophysics, particle physics, or physics education.

name: Psychology
about: All core areas of psychology, from the brain to society, with a strong grounding in statistics and research methods and skills training in small mentor-led groups. The English track has the same content as the Dutch one.

name: Religious Studies
about: How religion shapes lives and societies, studied through history, anthropology, sociology, psychology, political science and philosophy, on topics such as migration, radicalisation and climate, at a non-denominational faculty.

name: Spatial Planning and Design
about: Planning and designing living environments: physical and institutional design, water management, infrastructure, environmental planning and spatial software, with excursions to see real projects and a closing research project.
